newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA's Peugeot to present job cut plan soon.
newsitem.headline: PSA's Peugeot to present job cut plan soon.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet said on Thursday that the Automobiles Peugeot car division would present a job reduction proposal for 1997 to the staff council in two to three weeks.
He said the objective was to make the departures voluntary.
The Automobiles Citroen division this week presented a plan for 1,182 job cuts -- 800 through early retirement and other incentive plans and 382 through internal transfers.
"We expect in the next 15 days to three weeks to present a plan for Peugeot," Calvet told a news conference.
PSA Peugeot Citroen employed 139,100 people last year, compared with 139,900 in 1995.
"The group's strategy...aims to gradually, year after year, reduce staff on a voluntary basis to the extent possible," Calvet said.
Six weeks ago Renault SA announced plans to close a plant in Belgium employing 3,100 people and cut nearly 2,800 jobs in France this year. It employed just over 141,000 people in 1996.
